condition: Raised clinic blood pressure — confirm before diagnosing hypertension
permutationLabel: Man aged 49, clinic BP 152/94 at a wellness visit
summary: 49-year-old man at a wellness visit with clinic BP 152/94 and 148/92 on repeat, no symptoms, no known hypertension. NICE NG136: confirm with ABPM (or HBPM), assess cardiovascular risk and target-organ damage.

inputs.hpi: Asymptomatic 49-year-old man at a wellness visit. Clinic BP 152/94, repeated after 5 minutes 148/92. No headache, no chest pain, no visual disturbance. Never told his BP was high. Father had a stroke at 70.

exam.general: Well. BMI 29. BP 152/94 then 148/92 (right arm), 150/92 (left arm). Pulse 76 regular.
exam.cardiovascular: Heart sounds normal, no carotid bruits.

inputs.socialHistory: Office manager. Non-smoker. Alcohol 10 units/week. Sedentary.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Raised clinic blood pressure — suspected hypertension (unconfirmed)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Clinic BP 148–152/92–94 on two readings, asymptomatic. Suspected stage 1 hypertension: confirm with ambulatory (or home) BP monitoring; cardiovascular risk and target-organ assessment (urine ACR, U&E, HbA1c, lipids, ECG, fundi).

mustInclude.note: NICE NG136: offer ABPM (HBPM if unsuitable) to confirm a clinic BP of 140/90–180/120. Graded as management because the engine emits these arranged tests as plan lines.

emergencyLevel.note: Stage 1 range without symptoms: routine confirmation, not same-day.

mustNotAlarm.note: An asymptomatic screening visit must not raise an "emergency now" banner (alarm fatigue; front desk would redirect a well person).

guideline.name: NICE NG136 — hypertension in adults: diagnosis and management
guideline.section: Clinic BP 140/90–180/120: offer ambulatory (or home) BP monitoring to confirm the diagnosis; assess cardiovascular risk and target organ damage (urine albumin:creatinine ratio, haematuria, HbA1c, U&E/eGFR, lipids, fundoscopy, ECG); ≥ 180/120 with retinal haemorrhage or papilloedema (accelerated hypertension) or life-threatening symptoms: same-day specialist referral
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Hypertension in adults: diagnosis and management. NICE guideline NG136, 2019 (updated 2023).

guideline.name: 2017 ACC/AHA guideline — prevention, detection, evaluation and management of high blood pressure in adults
guideline.section: Out-of-office BP measurement (ABPM/HBPM) to confirm the diagnosis; hypertensive emergency: admission to an intensive care unit, controlled reduction of BP
guideline.citation: Whelton PK, Carey RM, Aronow WS, et al. 2017 ACC/AHA/AAPA/ABC/ACPM/AGS/APhA/ASH/ASPC/NMA/PCNA guideline for the prevention, detection, evaluation, and management of high blood pressure in adults. Hypertension. 2018;71:e13–e115.

rationale: A raised clinic reading needs out-of-office confirmation before a lifelong diagnosis, with cardiovascular risk and target-organ assessment. Negated symptoms ("no chest pain, no headache") must not escalate the visit.
